description: issue #864 (review round 1): `tell` is a COMMAND, so it keeps its callable form -- the boundary that stops the new value-position rule from over-reaching. `spec/turtles-and-sprites.md`'s canonical-forms table is authoritative for the C3 Sprites rows and gives `tell <turtle|turtle-list>` Kind **C**, while `ask` and `each` are Kind **S**; `spec/grammar.md:412` names it in the same terms -- `the Sprites command tell -- a mode switch that takes no block`. `spec/grammar.md:394` matches a keyword as `callable-name` `only where the C3 primitive matrix also gives that word a callable form`, and a command HAS one, so `( tell :t )` is a legitimate `parenthesized-call` exactly as `( forward 5 )` is. The first revision of #864's rule rejected all seven profile words alike and turned this very source -- which checked CLEAN before the rule existed -- into an `ol-bad-token`; a review caught it, and this fixture is the stack-neutral guard so no future slice re-broadens the rule by accident. Both spellings are asserted in one program: the parenthesized call on line 2 and the bare statement form on line 4, each followed by a turtle command so the addressed-set change has something to apply to. Its Kind-S siblings in the same profile are asserted in `statement-heads-not-values`; the pair is what pins the rule to the C3 Kind column rather than to profile membership. NOTE: two things about `tell` remain undiagnosed, and neither is a derivation error, so neither belongs to #864. `print tell` is a ZERO-INPUT call of a one-input command, so what it is missing is `ol-not-enough-inputs` from `checker-arity.ts` -- `tell` escapes that rule only because `spritesPrimitiveArity("tell")` is undefined. `print ( tell :t )` supplies the input and still uses a COMMAND AS A VALUE, which is a no-value question rather than an arity one and which OpenLogo answers for no Kind-C command today (`print ( forward 10 )` is equally undiagnosed; the parenthesized spelling is deliberate, since it supplies every required input and so isolates command-as-value from the missing-input case, which a bare `print forward` would not) -- a language-wide pre-existing hole, not something about `tell`. This is a check-mode fixture: it proves static legality only and does not execute.
